label: dense background; strongest after an o has been input (decaying o trace)
explanation: Dense feature: active on ~50% of all steps in ~99% of sequences, mostly at low magnitude spread evenly across phases, positions, L and tokens. The one clear structure is the letter o: an o input in the original phase almost always activates it (precision 0.985), runs of o (o o o) give the maximum activations, and activation then decays over the following steps (prev_tok=o and prev2_tok=o lifts 1.4x and 1.6x) and partly reappears in the copy phase around the steps where o is re-fed or about to be output (next_out=o lift 1.5x). The predicate o input now or earlier covers ~48% of activation mass and ~60% of the top activation quartile, at precision ~0.7 against a 0.5 base rate. The remaining roughly half of the mass is weak, widespread firing on sequences with no o, which I could not tie to any token, position or phase variable. It does not depend on copy correctness, digit count or token repetition.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=4: o, a, m, i; t=0: o, a, v, x; t=3: o, m, a, i) and the input two steps back (most: o, m, a, 3, i, g; least: t, 1, s, y); timing cues that raise it most: t=0, L=4 & t=7, L=7 & t=8.
